title: Implement git_repos scanner for Linux/macOS with tests
description:
Create lua/omni/scanners/git_repos.lua and spec/omni/scanners/git_repos_spec.lua following TDD.

Linux/macOS path (when target_triple does not contain 'windows'):
- Construct find command: find <path> -maxdepth <max_depth> -type d -name .git
- Call wezterm.run_child_process({'find', path, '-maxdepth', tostring(max_depth), '-type', 'd', '-name', '.git'})
- Parse stdout: each line is a .git dir path; strip /.git suffix to get project path
- Build entries: id=project_path, label=relative path from source base, workspace_name=label with dots→underscores
- Failed run_child_process → log_warn, return {}
- Empty output → return {}

Register via scanners.register('git_repos', git_repos_scanner).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Constructs correct find command with max_depth
- [ ] Parses stdout lines and strips /.git suffix
- [ ] Labels are relative to source base path
- [ ] workspace_name has dots replaced with underscores
- [ ] max_depth defaults to 5 when not specified
- [ ] Failed child process returns {} with warning
- [ ] Empty find output returns {}
- [ ] Registered in scanner registry as 'git_repos'

title: Implement grandchildren scanner with tests
description:
Create lua/omni/scanners/grandchildren.lua and spec/omni/scanners/grandchildren_spec.lua following TDD.

scan(source) does a two-level walk:
1. wezterm.read_dir(source.path) → group directories
2. For each group: wezterm.read_dir(group) → name directories

Returns entries for second-level directories:
- id = name absolute path
- label = basename(source.path) .. '/' .. basename(group) .. '/' .. basename(name)
- workspace_name = label with dots replaced by underscores

Skips non-directory entries at both levels.
Missing source or group paths → log_warn, skip.

Register via scanners.register('grandchildren', grandchildren_scanner).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Returns entries for second-level subdirectories
- [ ] Labels follow format: source_basename/group_basename/name_basename
- [ ] Skips intermediate grouping level in output (groups are not entries)
- [ ] workspace_name has dots replaced with underscores
- [ ] Missing source path logs warning and returns {}
- [ ] Missing/empty group directories handled gracefully
- [ ] Registered in scanner registry as 'grandchildren'

title: Create agent conventions and development guide
description:
Create a CONVENTIONS.md (or CLAUDE.md) that bridges the specs into actionable patterns for agents working on the codebase.

## Context
The specs/ directory has thorough design documentation, but an agent starting a new task needs a concise guide: "here's how we structure code, here's the error pattern, here's how to add a scanner." Without this, agents read specs piecemeal and may miss conventions, leading to inconsistent code that requires human correction. Per the architectural principles: "every review correction that could have been a permanent codebase signal is a missed opportunity."

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` exists at project root (Claude Code loads this automatically)
- [ ] Documents the module structure with clear orchestration vs primitive distinction:
  - Orchestration: `omni.init` (decides flow, sequences work)
  - Primitives: everything else (does work, returns output, no opinion on what happens next)
- [ ] Documents the error handling pattern:
  - Hard errors: `error("omni.wezterm: ...")` with context (source index, field name, expected vs actual)
  - Soft warnings: `wezterm.log_warn(...)` and skip/return empty
  - Where to use which (config validation = hard, missing path = soft)
- [ ] Documents how to add a new scanner type:
  1. Create `lua/omni/scanners/{name}.lua`
  2. Export `M.scan(source) -> ProjectEntry[]`
  3. Register in `scanners/init.lua`
  4. Add to valid types list in `config.lua` validation
  5. Create `spec/omni/scanners/{name}_spec.lua`
  6. Scanner must return entries with all 3 fields: `id`, `label`, `workspace_name`
- [ ] Documents the `ProjectEntry` contract (3 fields, what each means)
- [ ] Documents naming conventions (domain-oriented naming, not technical)
- [ ] Documents testing conventions (black-box, trophy model, test contracts not internals)
- [ ] References specs/ for detailed design rationale (doesn't duplicate them)
- [ ] Concise — under 150 lines. This is a quick-reference, not a novel.

## Notes
This is the highest-leverage context engineering investment. One well-placed conventions doc prevents hundreds of corrections downstream.
close_reason: CLAUDE.md created at project root (100 lines). Covers all acceptance criteria: module structure with orchestration/primitive labels, error handling patterns, scanner addition checklist, ProjectEntry contract, naming and testing conventions. References specs/ for detail.

title: Add lint and format checks to lefthook pre-commit
description:
Extend the existing lefthook pre-commit hook to run luacheck and stylua as automated backpressure.

## Context
lefthook.yml exists with a beads pre-commit hook. Adding lint/format checks ensures agents (and humans) get immediate feedback on every commit attempt. This is the tightest feedback loop available without CI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `lefthook.yml` pre-commit includes a `luacheck` command that runs `luacheck lua/ spec/`
- [ ] `lefthook.yml` pre-commit includes a `stylua` command that runs `stylua --check lua/ spec/`
- [ ] Both commands run in parallel with the existing beads hook
- [ ] A commit with lint errors is rejected (non-zero exit blocks commit)
- [ ] A commit with format violations is rejected
- [ ] Commands only run when `.lua` files are staged (use `glob` or `run` filter to avoid running on non-Lua changes)

## Notes
Depends on luacheck/stylua config files existing first.

title: Add luacheck and stylua configuration files
description:

## Context
The devenv Dockerfile (omni_wezterm-wue) installs luacheck, busted, and stylua but no config files exist yet. Without config files, these tools either don't run or use defaults that may not match project conventions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.luacheckrc` exists at project root with:
  - `std` set to `lua54` (WezTerm uses Lua 5.4)
  - `globals` includes `wezterm` and any WezTerm-specific globals
  - `read_globals` for busted globals (`describe`, `it`, `assert`, `before_each`, `after_each`, `setup`, `teardown`, `pending`, `spy`, `stub`, `mock`)
  - Sensible max line length (120 or similar)
  - `exclude_files` for `.devenv/`, `.beads/`, `tmp/`
- [ ] `stylua.toml` exists at project root with:
  - Indent style matching project convention (2-space indent is Lua standard)
  - Quote style set (prefer double quotes to match WezTerm conventions)
  - Column width matching luacheck max line length
- [ ] `luacheck lua/` runs cleanly (no errors) against any existing source files
- [ ] `stylua --check lua/` runs cleanly against any existing source files
- [ ] Both tools also cover `spec/` directory

## Notes
This enables the lefthook pre-commit hook to be extended with lint/format checks (separate issue).

title: Add scanner contract validation in scanners registry
description:
Add runtime validation in scanners/init.lua that verifies scanner return values conform to the ProjectEntry contract.

## Context
The ProjectEntry contract (id, label, workspace_name) is documented in specs but not enforced programmatically. If an agent writes a new scanner that returns entries missing a field or with wrong types, the bug surfaces later (in the UI or workspace switching) rather than at the scanner boundary. Per the principles: "fail fast and visibly" and "breaking changes impossible to miss."

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scanners/init.lua` exports a `dispatch(source)` function that:
  1. Looks up the scanner by `source.type`
  2. Calls `scanner.scan(source)`
  3. Validates each returned entry has: `id` (string), `label` (string), `workspace_name` (string)
  4. Raises an error if any entry is malformed (with scanner type and entry index in the message)
- [ ] `discovery.lua` uses `scanners.dispatch(source)` instead of calling scanners directly
- [ ] Validation error message includes: scanner type, entry index, which field is missing/wrong
  - Example: `"omni.wezterm: scanner 'children' returned invalid entry #2: missing field 'workspace_name'"`
- [ ] Tests verify that malformed scanner output is caught:
  - Missing field raises error
  - Wrong type (e.g., id = 42) raises error
  - Valid entries pass through unchanged

## Notes
This turns the documented contract into an executable constraint. Cost is minimal (one validation loop per scan), benefit is catching bugs at the source rather than downstream.

title: Label orchestration vs primitives in plugin-architecture spec
description:
Add explicit orchestration vs primitive labels to the module responsibilities section of specs/plugin-architecture.md.

## Context
The architectural principles emphasize keeping orchestration (decides/sequences) separate from primitives (does/transforms). The current spec implicitly follows this — omni.init is orchestration, everything else is primitives — but doesn't label it explicitly. An agent modifying a module might accidentally add decision-making logic to a primitive, or add data transformation logic to the orchestrator.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each module in the "Module Responsibilities" section has a clear tag: `[orchestration]` or `[primitive]`
- [ ] A brief note explains the distinction: "Primitives transform data and return output. Orchestration sequences work and makes decisions. Keep them separate."
- [ ] `omni.init` is labeled `[orchestration]`
- [ ] `omni.config`, `omni.discovery`, `omni.scanners.*`, `omni.workspace`, `omni.ui`, `omni.path` are labeled `[primitive]`
- [ ] The note clarifies that `omni.discovery` is a *composed primitive* (combines scanner results) not orchestration (it doesn't decide what to do with the results)

## Notes
Small change, high signal. Takes 5 minutes, prevents category confusion in every future agent session.

title: Add GitHub Actions CI workflow
description:
Add a minimal CI pipeline that runs tests and linting on every push and PR, providing automated backpressure before human review.

## Context
Currently there is no CI. Agent-written code has no automated verification beyond local pre-commit hooks. CI catches drift that slips past local hooks (e.g., agent forgot to run hooks, or worked in a context without lefthook).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` exists with a workflow that triggers on push and pull_request
- [ ] Workflow installs Lua 5.4, luarocks, busted, luacheck
- [ ] Workflow runs `luacheck lua/ spec/` and fails on errors
- [ ] Workflow runs `busted spec/` and fails on test failures
- [ ] Workflow runs `stylua --check lua/ spec/` and fails on format violations
- [ ] Workflow uses caching for luarocks dependencies (to keep CI fast)
- [ ] Workflow runs on ubuntu-latest (Linux is the primary dev platform)
- [ ] Badge can be added to README (optional, not required)

## Notes
This is the "CI as backpressure" principle — every check that runs on agent PRs is a feedback signal. Keep the pipeline fast (under 2 minutes ideally).
